title: Three Terms and One Short Tube
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：oxygen　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 oxygen 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the researcher ① breathed the oxygen that no student in the lab would have described, and he said the breathing was the whole of the term. The ② oxygen, meaning the gas itself and not the tube, ran three terms and stayed undescribed in the book; oxygen, he said, is the only thing in a lab that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ sample of oxygen in that lab had the same short tube beside it, and the ④ oxygen at the far bench, meaning the sample they kept for the children to test and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Oxygen, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the researcher said the describing is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the oxygen was the whole of the matter, meaning the life and not the gas. The ⑥ oxygen, meaning the life and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; oxygen, he said, is either something you breathe or the only word that means both gas and a life. He said the life is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ oxygen had become a line in a paper, and the paper had become an argument about the short tube. The ⑧ oxygen of the whole thing, the researcher wrote in February, was one lab and three terms of describing; oxygen, he said, is either the sample at the far bench or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ oxygen I remember is the oxygen described in the paper, which closed in 1967 and is still described as the quietest in the lab. ⑩ Oxygen, my mother said in 1969, is the only thing that improves by being described; all oxygen, she said, is a life that has agreed to look like gas. She said the life was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 氧气（指实验室里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 氧气（指那口氧气本身，与细细的试管相对）
C. 固定搭配：breathe the oxygen 呼吸这一口氧气
D. n. 氧气（指留给孩子们测的那一份）
E. n. 氧气之事（抽象总称，指一处实验室的氧气之事）
F. n. 氧气（指研究报告里写到、被描述的那一口）
G. n. 氧气、生气（指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 生气（抽象总称，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: breathed the oxygen that no student in the lab would have described
The oxygen, meaning the gas itself and not the tube
Every sample of oxygen in that lab
the oxygen at the far bench
the oxygen was the whole of the matter
the oxygen had become a line in a paper
The oxygen of the whole thing

answers.why: breathe the oxygen 意为“呼吸这一口氧气”，1960 年那位研究员把实验室里没有一位学生肯描述的一口氧气做了一遍。
oxygen 意为“氧气”，指那口氧气本身而不是细细的试管，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被描述。
oxygen 意为“氧气”，指实验室里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一支细细的试管。
oxygen 意为“氧气”，指最远那张实验台的留给孩子们测的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
oxygen 意为“氧气、生气”，指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这口生气就是那件事的全部。
oxygen 意为“生气”，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西而不是那口氧气，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
oxygen 意为“氧气”，指研究报告里写到、被描述的那一口，到 1965 年这一口成了研究报告里的一行。
oxygen 意为“氧气之事”，研究员二月写道，整件事的氧气之事是一处实验室和三个学期的描述。
oxygen 意为“氧气”，我记得的是研究报告里描述过的那一口，1967 年测定了，至今仍被说成实验室里最安静的一口。
oxygen 为抽象总称，母亲 1969 年说，氧气是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的氧气。

叔叔说这口生气就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那口氧气。（oxygen）
